title: Fluent SDK transactional apply and snapshot rollback for Optimize automation
creator: Aisha Kline
description:
Problem: Customers using Optimize automation need a clear, developer-friendly SDK and API surface to commit batching/caching recommendations safely and revert them reliably when regressions or incidents occur. Current internal endpoints are low-level and require orchestration glue; operators have runbooks that are error-prone for partial failures or duplicate deliveries.

Goal: Implement a fluent SDK + control-plane API that exposes a transactional commit model with lightweight snapshotting and idempotent commit tokens, plus a snapshot-based rollback endpoint and first-class webhook semantics for downstream systems. The surface should make it easy for platform teams to: (1) propose recommendations, (2) dry-run and preview cost/latency impacts, (3) commit with a single idempotent call, and (4) revert to a stored snapshot if quality/regression signals trigger.

Design summary:
- API: /optimize/v1/transactions (POST) to create a transaction and store a snapshot; returns transaction_id and idempotency_key. /optimize/v1/transactions/{id}/commit (POST) to atomically apply recommended config changes. /optimize/v1/transactions/{id}/rollback (POST) to restore snapshot. Commit/rollback are idempotent: clients must provide idempotency_token; service stores outcomes for 7 days and returns canonical result on retry.
- SDK: fluent transaction builder (Transaction.create, .addRecommendation, .preview(), .commit({idempotencyToken}), .rollback()). SDK will surface partial apply errors as structured diagnostics and expose async hooks for webhook events.
- Webhooks: on transaction lifecycle events (created, previewed, committed, rolled_back, failed) with at-least-once delivery, backoff, and DLQ. Payload includes transaction metadata, diff, cost delta estimate, and checksum of applied config. Webhook fanout should be limited per-customer to avoid thundering herd; provide batching capability.
- Snapshot model: store reified configuration and pre-apply KV/caching state metadata (ttl, cache keys) to enable safe revert. Snapshots are immutable and reference-counted; automatic garbage collection after retention window (90 days default).
- Safety & observability: built-in dry-run for preview, canary commit flag (percentage rollout), automatic regression guard that can trigger rollback using evaluation hooks. Expose metrics: transaction.commit.latency, transaction.rollback.count, transaction.duplicates.replayed, transaction.failure_reason.

Acceptance criteria:
1) SDK users can commit and re-run commit without double-applying (idempotency verified in integration tests).
2) Rollback restores pre-apply state within SLO for 95% of test cases.
3) Webhooks deliver lifecycle events and DLQ receives non-deliverable payloads.
4) End-to-end demo: create recommendations, preview cost delta, commit with canary, and programmatically rollback based on a simulated quality trigger.

Implementation plan:
- Phase 1 (API+Database): transaction and snapshot storage, idempotency table, basic commit/rollback handlers (2 sprints).
- Phase 2 (SDK + Webhooks): fluent SDK surfaced in JS/Python, webhook delivery service with DLQ (1 sprint).
- Phase 3 (Safety & Rollouts): canary rollout integration, regression hooks, monitoring and runbook updates (1 sprint).

Migration: new SDK will default to transaction path; existing internal automations can call compatibility endpoint /optimize/v1/legacy-apply which will translate into a transaction under-the-hood for easier migration.

Risks: snapshot size for large config trees, long-tail of rollback failures when external systems have drift; mitigation: snapshot pruning, pre-commit validation hooks, and required eventual consistency checks.
comments: 2025-02-13 - Initial scoping and stakeholder sync (PM, DX, Infra). Agreed on transaction-first model and snapshot retention defaults.

2025-02-17 - Design review with Runtime team: kernel-level cache state can't be fully materialized for every config; refined snapshot to include deterministic cache keys + version markers instead of full blob.
2025-02-21 - UX review: Console team requested a transaction timeline view and direct rollback button; opened PM follow-up: PM-4102.
2025-02-26 - Security review kickoff: need KMS encryption for snapshot blobs and audit log entries for commit/rollback (SSE + access-control).
2025-03-04 - Integration tests added for idempotency replay cases; found race when simultaneous commit+rollback attempted, added optimistic locking and retry policy.
Reviewer feedback (2025-03-04): please add an explicit webhook schema version and include consumer retry-backoff guidance in docs (see docs link).
